text:
**Short answer: Starling is the better all-rounder for most people; Monzo is better if you want richer budgeting tools and a more feature-packed app.**

| | **Starling** | **Monzo** |
|---|---|---|
| Monthly fee | Free | Free; optional paid plans |
| Spending abroad | No Starling fees for card spending or cash withdrawals | No foreign card-spending fees; cash-withdrawal limits can apply, especially outside the EEA |
| Cash deposits | Free up to £1,000 per calendar year, then a charge applies | Usually £1 per deposit; some paid plans include free deposits |
| Budgeting | Spaces and spending insights | Pots and more extensive budgeting features |
| Savings | Linked savings options; rates vary | Savings Pots and rates that can vary by plan and account |
| Protection | Eligible deposits covered by FSCS | Eligible deposits covered by FSCS |

**Choose Starling** if you travel, sometimes need cash, or want a straightforward free account with fewer withdrawal restrictions abroad.

**Choose Monzo** if budgeting features, Pots, or its wider app ecosystem matter more to you—and check the current plan terms before paying for extras.

Both are UK-licensed banks, and eligible deposits are protected by the FSCS up to the applicable limit. Savings rates and fees change, so verify the latest terms before switching. A common practical choice is to keep your existing account and try one of them as a second account first.
